scope: All nine Mellan tee sites: existing physical platforms, nominal card references and route starts in 40 m buffered native-source windows.
method: Direct visual review of native 0.16 m RGB images and exactly projected existing outlines. Distances measured independently with pyproj EPSG:3006 and Shapely point-to-polygon distance. No image registration fit or automatic boundary extraction.

reviews.note: Four existing platforms are identifiable: northeast upper, northeast lower, west of the path and southwest. Their outlines follow visible turf within edge/shadow uncertainty. The nominal rear references enter woodland, the fourth lies on the path and the shortest lies in scrub southwest of the forward platform. Three rear platforms cannot be assigned to tee identities from imagery alone. The southwest pad is a plausible fourth-group candidate by spatial/card ordering; the shortest group has no separately identified pad.

reviews.note: Four distinct west-to-east platforms agree with existing footprints; the western end is partly shadowed. The reference sequence increases eastward but three groups fall between or outside the physical pads. Ordered candidate associations follow the four separate platforms; nearest-pad assignment alone would attach the third reference to the preceding platform.

routeStartDiagnostic.assessment: Pre-alignment route diagnostic; downstream adoption is governed by explicit reference decisions.

reviews.note: The southern platform and the additional northern platform are visible among rock, scrub and tree shadow. Existing boundaries are retained because obscured edge details do not support a new outline. The longest pair falls in scrub well south of the southern pad. The middle pair lies just south of that pad, yet the card-group progression could instead use the northern pad; that association remains uncertain. The shortest reference lies beside the path northeast of the northern pad.

reviews.note: The west, middle and east platforms agree with the observed turf. The first reference is inside the east pad; the middle pair lies just south of the middle pad; the last pair lies on the west pad edge. Tree shadows obscure parts of the southern edges, so no new boundary is inferred.

limitations: The large displacement is mainly in nominal card references, not a common offset of physical turf outlines.

The imagery does not identify daily marker colours/numbers. Explicit align-to-observed-pad decisions place displayed references on supported physical platforms; they do not establish actual daily marker positions.
Shortest tee references at H2, H3, H4 and H6 have no separately identified physical platform in these windows.
H6 rear-platform and H8 middle/short-group associations remain unresolved; nearest-pad assignment alone is insufficient.
Retained boundaries include shadow uncertainty. This is not a complete census of every historical, seasonal or forward tee position.
2025-06-14 imagery cannot verify changes completed after that capture.
